title: CS2 Beginner Guide: Crosshair, Utility and Team Economy
summary: Learn Counter-Strike 2 fundamentals: crosshair placement, grenade timing, teammate trades, team buys and useful communication.
intro: Better Counter-Strike 2 play begins with positioning and decisions, not only faster reactions. A team that shares information, buys together and supports each other's fights can outperform a group of individually talented players who take isolated duels. These fundamentals work across maps, even when balance changes make specific weapon prices or grenade lineups outdated.

sections.heading: Begin each round with a simple team plan
paragraphs: During freeze time, decide whether the team will contest an area, gather information or attempt a fast objective. A short call is more useful than several competing strategies. Identify who will lead the first contact, who can support and who watches the back. You can adjust the plan as information arrives, but teammates need an initial expectation.

On defense, avoid abandoning a site based only on a teammate seeing one opponent. Enemy presence does not necessarily reveal the full attack. Share the number of players you actually observed, the utility heard and whether you saw the bomb. Clear facts help defenders decide whether to hold, rotate or delay.

sections.heading: Use crosshair placement to reduce difficult flicks
paragraphs: Keep your crosshair near the height and position where an enemy might appear. When moving through a doorway, trace likely angles instead of pointing at the floor. You reduce the distance required to adjust when a defender becomes visible. Practice clearing one position at a time while using cover to avoid exposing yourself to several angles simultaneously.

Movement matters as well. Learn how weapon accuracy changes while moving and practice stopping before precise shots when appropriate. Do not rely on crouching as a cure for every missed bullet. A repeatable routine combining angle clearing, controlled movement and deliberate firing is a better foundation than constantly changing your crosshair settings.

sections.heading: Know what each grenade is meant to achieve
paragraphs: A smoke obscures vision and can isolate a dangerous angle, but it does not provide physical protection from bullets. Avoid walking blindly through it without a teammate who can cover the exit. A flashbang can help someone enter a contested space if it is timed so the attacker is ready to act. Throwing one randomly can also disrupt teammates.

Other utility can pressure opponents away from cover or slow a rush. Think about the outcome you need before using any grenade: deny a sightline, force a reposition or create a safe timing window. Tell teammates when you plan to throw it. Exact lineups and effects can change through updates, so verify them in your current game build.

sections.heading: Stay close enough to trade a teammate
paragraphs: A teammate trade happens when a second player can challenge the opponent immediately after the first player is eliminated. Supporting an entry requires being close enough to respond, but not standing directly on top of the person ahead. Good spacing preserves your line of sight and avoids blocking movement. Even a lost first duel can create useful information.

After an encounter, communicate the enemy's last known position and any confirmed information. Keep the call short. A statement such as one opponent at the doorway is more helpful than an emotional explanation of how unfair the fight felt. Your surviving teammates still need to hear footsteps and coordinate their own moves.

sections.heading: Treat team money as a shared resource
paragraphs: Before purchasing expensive gear, check teammate money and discuss whether the group can make a coordinated buy. One fully equipped player alongside several teammates who cannot support a push may be less effective than a team with a coherent budget. Some rounds are better approached with a planned save or lower-cost purchase to protect future options.

Include utility in the decision rather than automatically spending everything on the most expensive weapon. On defense, consider whether equipment helps you hold or retake a site. Prices, purchase availability and economy details may change, so use the current buy menu and round information instead of trusting an old internet chart.

sections.heading: A repeatable routine for improvement
paragraphs: In practice, trace common corners at approximate head height and clear them without rushing. Learn one useful smoke and flash on a map you actually play, then practice their timing with a teammate. After a lost round, identify one avoidable mistake: an isolated duel, late support, a confused rotation or an inconsistent team buy.

Do not try to memorize every tactical setup at once. A player who reliably communicates, aims at likely positions and supports teammates will have a stronger base for advanced utility later. Revisit grenade lineups after map updates and use the game itself to confirm they still work.
points: Agree on the opening intention during freeze time.
Place your crosshair where an opponent could appear.
Use flashes and smokes for a specific teammate action.
Support trades without crowding another player.
Coordinate purchases using current team funds.
